# dlansp

> Returns the value of the one-norm, Frobenius norm, infinity-norm, or the largest absolute value of any element of a real symmetric matrix supplied in packed storage.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlansp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlansp';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlansp( order, norm, uplo, N, AP, WORK ) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout |
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  |  | specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part is packed ('upper' or 'lower') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed symmetric matrix, length >= N*(N+1)/2 |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out |  |  | workspace array, length >= N |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANSP as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the symmetric matrix A is supplied.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part of A is supplied
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part of A is supplied
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANSP is set to zero.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlansp.ndarray(
    norm, uplo,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | specifies the norm: `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  |  | specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed symmetric matrix, length >= `N*(N+1)/2` |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AP` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | workspace array, length >= `N` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANSP as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the symmetric matrix A is supplied.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part of A is supplied
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part of A is supplied
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANSP is set to zero.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle

## Notes

-   `dlansp()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLANSP`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlansp.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlansp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlansp';

// 3x3 symmetric matrix in upper packed storage:

//   A = [  2.0   3.0  -1.0 ]

//       [  3.0   5.0   2.0 ]

//       [ -1.0   2.0   7.0 ]
const AP = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, -1.0, 2.0, 7.0 ] );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 3 );
let result;

result = dlansp( 'column-major', 'max', 'upper', 3, AP, WORK );
console.log( 'Max norm:', result );

result = dlansp( 'column-major', 'one-norm', 'upper', 3, AP, WORK );
console.log( 'One norm:', result );

result = dlansp( 'column-major', 'inf-norm', 'upper', 3, AP, WORK );
console.log( 'Inf norm:', result );

result = dlansp( 'column-major', 'frobenius', 'upper', 3, AP, WORK );
console.log( 'Frobenius norm:', result );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLANSP`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLANSP returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a real symmetric matrix A, supplied in packed form.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{DLANSP} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(A(i,j))) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
